newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zwickel-IG Metall no great expectations from talks.
newsitem.headline: Zwickel-IG Metall no great expectations from talks.

text.p: IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel said on Monday he was entering emergency talks over plans to cut back on sick pay with employers with "no great expectations" of a quick agreement.

"When you consider that 150,000 workers in the metal industry last week protested over this, it shows the level of indignation and rage that workers feel over this. In such a situation any solution will be complicated," Zwickel said.
Zwickel was speaking to journalists as he arrived for a meeting with representatives of the employers' union Gesamtmetall.
Zwickel added that the union had "no interest in the situation escalating".
IG Metall vice-chairman Walter Riester, also arriving for the talks, re-affirmed that the union would only be talking about the issue of cuts in sick pay, rather than wider pay talks.

German unions have been angered by a new law reducing sick pay to 80 percent from 100 percent, aimed at cutting labour costs. The unions say such benefits have been hard won in negotiation and cannot be simply abolished overnight.
